name: level-ground-then-build
description: #1009: ordering `level_ground` over a rectangle of uneven ground queues excavation work for a qualified rock_digger driver instead of carving anything synchronously. For seed:42's default staffed map, the 2x2 rect (15,13)-(16,14) sits on a genuine two-voxel step (surface Y: 36,35 / 37,36) — exactly management_office tier1's own 2x2 footprint. `build management_office at:15,13` is refused first (baseline: #1008's placement levelness rule is live), then `level_ground minX:15 maxX:16 minZ:13 maxZ:14` is ordered and drained to completion via a `pendingActionCount`-gated wait, after which the identical build order succeeds. A TWO-voxel step, not one: #1008's refinement lets a footprint straddle a single voxel step (BUILDING_PLACEMENT_MAX_HEIGHT_SPREAD), so the one-voxel rect this file used to stand on — (14,17)-(15,18) — is now a legal placement and proved nothing about levelling. All three of these steps click through the real BuildMenu.ts controls (`makeTerrainSection`/`armLevelGroundTool` wired a genuine drag-a-rectangle tool, mirroring the ramp tool) rather than falling back to console commands — `role: 'player'` throughout. The excavation wait is bounded to 100 ticks rather than a flat `tick 200`: staffed payroll (PAY_CYCLE_TICKS=10, 5 salaried employees) legitimately drains cash every pay cycle it runs through, and a needlessly long fixed pad drove cash negative before the second build's $8,000 could be charged, refusing it for insufficient funds instead of proving the levelling.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): 5 employees (including two driving.excavator-qualified drivers) and 4 vehicles (including one rock_digger), matching STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION (balance.ts) — the same roster building-ramp-visual.json relies on for its own rock_digger work.

Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, one of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants, before ordering any excavation work. Mirrors building-ramp-visual.json's identical bootstrap step.

Baseline: the rect spans two voxel levels (Y: 36,35 / 37,36), past the one-level tolerance BUILDING_PLACEMENT_MAX_HEIGHT_SPREAD allows, so #1008's placement rule refuses the order outright — before any level_ground order exists to make this pass. Clicks through the real BuildMenu catalog + tile picker, then proves Confirm itself is unreachable on the uneven tile (#1045) rather than clicking it and asserting a refused command.

expect.note: issue #1045 — uneven footprint leaves Confirm disabled; no PlannedBuilding was queued for the uneven footprint.

steps.description: Order ground-levelling over the same uneven rect via the real BuildMenu control — armLevelGroundTool arms a rectangle drag exactly like armRampTool's line drag (makeTerrainSection, #1009).

expect.note: Order-time cost (4 excess voxels x LEVEL_GROUND_COST_PER_VOXEL) is charged immediately, mirroring build_ramp's own order-then-work pattern.

steps.description: Drain the queued level_ground work — a qualified rock_digger driver walks to the rect and carves the 4 excess voxels down to the lowest column. Gated on pendingActionCount reaching 0 (the level_ground action is the only one in flight at this point) rather than a flat `tick 200`: padding far past the job's own duration needlessly burns staffed payroll (PAY_CYCLE_TICKS=10) against the second build's $8,000 below.

The identical build order that was refused before levelling now succeeds — the rect is dead flat once the level_ground action has landed. Clicks through the real BuildMenu catalog + tile picker again.

expect.note: Accepted and queued for construction — proves the levelled area now passes #1008's placement rule.
